questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to study at the Complutense, because of the courses that were offered that I found very interesting and useful as well as the fact that I have wanted to be able to stay in the Spanish capital over a longer period of time and the semester abroad was the perfect opportunity to be able to live out that dream.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am extremely satisfied overall with my study abroad experience in Madrid as well as thankful for what I have learned both academically and personally and for the people that have been part of making my exchange an unforgettable experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Well, I would not say it was too difficult or too easy. The International Relations Office at the University was helpful with the general process, but getting to understand how exactly certain things work in an academic setting in Spain took some time in the beginning, but I view that as part of the learning process and never imagined that I would receive a piece of paper telling me everything I needed to know from day one. My experience was that if I sought out information either at the university office or among my Spanish peers, most of my questions would be answered.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help from the International Relations Office to enroll me as an exchange student.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: In my case, I ended up looking a bit late, around November with a good friend of mine, who was also going to Madrid to study abroad. Therefore I was not only looking for a place for myself to stay but also a place where my friend could stay. We ended up finding a place through the website Spotahome. My recommendation will be to look as early as possible and check out different sites online.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you are not used to living with roommates, you better accustom yourself quickly as the vast majority of students living off campus share apartments with roommates. I shared with a total of 6 people. Set some ground rules in the beginning and show respect for one another. If one or more roommates do not follow certain ground rules that make you feel uncomfortable, talk to them and explain how you feel. At the end of the day, almost everyone wants to get along, especially when you are going to live with each other for months.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have read about some type of On-Campus housing through the University Complutense called Halls of Residence, but I have not been informed by the University through our email correspondence nor did I ever meet anyone who actually lives there. It does not seem to be that big of a thing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Well, I was told by the UCM that as an Erasmus student, my registration process began with me trying out different classes and deciding which ones I liked. Therefore handing out a document to every individual professor getting their signature and then handing it all to the International Relations Office. Apparently, this was not all factual, as I was told by KU that I could only be enrolled in the courses where I had gotten a Forhåndsgodkendelse. After having realized this, I had to talk to KU about getting a revideret forhåndsgodkendelse. The only problem was that the deadline had exactly just passed even though I had only been at the uni for a few days. Luckily KU helped and we resolved it so that I could get the courses that I actually found interesting and not just the ones that I had selected at home in Denmark without having had a chance to be sure that the level was right for me as well as the content.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think I answer this above.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I answer this above.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to both of your Universities from the beginning and figure out whether the information you receive is the same or not. I did not receive the same information from the beginning which created a moment of stress for me in the registration process, but I am happy that it worked out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses were just exactly to my liking. Additionally, the professors were very sympathetic which made me feel welcome as the only exchange student, which I was in 4/5 of my courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In most courses, there was less teacher-student interaction in the class. At KU and in Denmark in general we have a long tradition of valuing what students think about a certain topic and students get to be very much involved in the classroom conversation. Whereas in Spain, for the most part, it is much more a teacher monologue, and as a student you just sit back, listen, and take notes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ESTRUCTURA Y SISTEMA MUNDIAL DE LA INFORMACIÓN (803634)
I would recommend any future student with an interest in studying abroad at the Faculty of Infomation Sciences to enroll in this course. Sergio Principe is probably the most sympathetic and friendly teacher that I have ever had. He is extremely knowledgeable about current world affairs, politics, media theories, etc. He always teaches in an energetic matter which is why his classes are never boring. I have learned so incredibly much during his course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Trips to other cities or abroad. Being on Erasmus you find yourself in a situation where you want to explore not only your study destination but also surrounding cities or even countries. I ended up going to places that I did not plan to go to.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The cost of transportation in Madrid was way lower than I could have ever imagined. I pay only 8€ a month for my youth card which allows me to travel freely by bus, metro, and train in all of the Capital region, as far as Toledo. In Denmark the youth card cost close to 10 times as much, or 80€.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The uni did offer certain conferences or excursions, but being very busy with my own private life, I did not pay too much attention to what was being offered.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I answer this above.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Depending on each one's interest, in the city of Madrid, there is an abundance of opportunities. Going to the Retiro Park with friends for a picnic, taking a swim in the public swimming pools on a hot day, strolling through the streets of the city center, and eating tapas at the bars or food markets. Madrid is a city where you really get to understand what living life means.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy as I have previously spent half a year living in Malaga, Andalucia where I learned about cultural barriers and was able to break them down.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do not be shy. Talk to them. Let them know that you are open to friendships. Do not expect everyone to come to you and do the talking. You have to do the work, at least in the beginning.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A classic of Spain is the siesta. Living a bit outside of the city center I have had to get used to not being able to go have a beverage or a tapas with friends at any time we wanted. We were all well aware of the siesta, but that doest not mean we like the idea that establishments are closed for multiple hours during the day. You change your habits a bit due to the environment where you find yourself.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The gastronomy, architecture, and laidbackness of the Spanish people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
First, look for accommodation as early as possible and research the neighborhoods and how far they are from uni. Madrid is a large city and the capital region has more inhabitants than our country of Denmark, so get used to longer distances and spending more time on transportation. 
Second, try to be as social as possible in the beginning. Both with your peers at uni as well as your roommates. The first impression you give to people is usually the one they remember the most. Also, join the events that Erasmus has to offer as well as other exchange student organizations such as City Life Madrid. By following my instructions you can be sure to meet like-minded people and make friendships. 
Third, focus on your studies. Studying abroad is not just fun, but a journey with its own challenges. Studying completely in Spanish is not easy and it takes time to get accustomed to it. Therefore go to your classes, hand in your papers, and try to absorb the language as much as you can in your free time. After one semester you will then see a big increase in your language skills.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I already answer this.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being in a Spanish academic setting learning how to navigate a new system and also just the daily interactions with peers, strangers, and roommates while living abroad.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Besides certain academic challenges, I would say that living with 6 people for 5 months has been a challenge at times, both positively and negatively. However, it has been rather rewarding in terms of the friendships established and getting to know me while living under collective norms and rules compared to living by my own rules.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
